gen-gf-paprika-gf-lexend: Paprika spreads its letters far apart, each with a counter like a hollow reed cut open. Lexend takes the smooth side, with oversized lowercase and open curves whose thickness never wavers.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-liter: Loud, widely spaced and full of attitude. Paprika earns its place on big, short lines, while Liter lines up behind it with marker-tip strokes of no contrast and wide round mouths.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-mada: Paprika spaces its letters far apart, each counter hollow like a cut reed. It handles commanding display work, while Mada leaves its curves open and gives text a towering midzone.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-maven-pro: Paprika scatters its letters apart and gives its lowercase the presence of capitals, counters breathing like a cut reed. Maven Pro quiets that loudness with level lines and a welcoming c.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-michroma: Paprika sets its letters well apart, with counters like a cut reed. Michroma gives each letter just as wide a berth, so both fonts share a spacious, daylight-filled openness.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-montserrat-underline: Commanding and expressive, Paprika spaces its letters far apart with hollow, reed-like counters. Montserrat Underline reads like tracing one thick thread, its round bowls never swelling or tapering across a paragraph.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-mozilla-headline: Expressive to the point of swagger, Paprika spreads its letters far apart and gives its lowercase real presence. Mozilla Headline handles the approachable side: big lowercase, splayed c terminals.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-mozilla-text: Paprika scatters its letters wide, with counters that breathe like a hollow reed cut open. Mozilla Text then reads with bold-looking lowercase and flared terminals, a steady texture across a paragraph.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-nobile: Contemporary meets expressive: Paprika spreads its letters well apart, counters breathing like a cut reed. Nobile keeps its capitals barely taller than lowercase, and open mouths give paragraphs a compact, orderly texture.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Paprika is the loud one, spacing its letters out and giving its lowercase capital-sized presence. Noto Kufi Arabic is the modern, clean counterpart, with a welcoming gap in the c and capitals barely above lowercase.
